thesis: Pluralism needs practical family compatibility; policy should remove structural penalties rather than select preferred people.
role: Turn counterexamples into institutional principle and retention arithmetic.

ideas.statement: Education and cognitive ability differ; reproductive correlations depend on cohorts, gender and institutions.
Reproductive neutrality of virtue removes structural penalties without prescribing who reproduces.
Cultural continuation depends on fertility, retention, survival and partnerships.
Coercive retention is morally distinct from voluntary shared care and belonging.

evidenceAndExamples.statement: Swedish male-register counterexample includes within-brother comparison.
Two imagined life paths illustrate distributed versus individualized parenting costs.
Illustrative population growth assumes no migration and high retention.

objectionsAndQualifications.statement: No inevitable dysgenic law; policies cannot justify coercive reproduction.
Fertility may converge, children leave and mixed marriages grow.

audit.notes: Entire assigned batch read; numbered subchapters covered; no independent citation verification.
